messages.author: 67ad43f188b9c5e7
messages.subject: get the Theta value of the highest point in the plot
parts:
Hi Phil,

I have been using mirt package so far and found it very helpful in my project! Recently I cam across a question, wherein I am interested in knowing the Theta value which corresponds to the highest point in the item information plot. I wanted to get that Theta value for all items in my item bank. I wonder if there is a command to output that in mirt package? 

I was using this code to output the item information plot: 
itemplot(model, 2, type = 'info')

and this is the output I got (and I am guessing the Theta value I want to get is roughly 0 at this case, when the y-axis reaches the highest point): 
Any help is appreciated!

Thanks in advance,
Yingyi

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: get the Theta value of the highest point in the plot
parts:
It's possible to obtain these information function via iteminfo(), and use function like optimize() to obtain the highest point via numerical searches. I'm sure there's analytical formula available in the literature, but I have not implemented these in mirt. 

Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: get the Theta value of the highest point in the plot
parts:
library(mirt)
mod <- mirt(Science, 1)
itemplot(mod, 2, type = 'info')

item2 <- extract.item(mod, 2)
fn <- function(theta) iteminfo(item2, Theta=theta)
opt <- optimize(fn, c(-6,6), maximum=TRUE)
opt

library(latticeExtra)
itemplot(mod, 2, type = 'info') + 
    layer(panel.points(opt$maximum, opt$objective, col = 'red', pch=16, cex = 1.5)) + 
    layer(panel.text(opt$maximum, opt$objective + .01, 'Max Info'))

Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: get the Theta value of the highest point in the plot
parts:
Most optimizers in R are only local searchers, so you should probably change the search range to something more feasible of the maximum. For this item, I would probably set the range to be between say -1 and 1 to ensure that the global optim is correctly located. HTH.

Phil
